reasoning: Both switch to snapshots and leave the profiler alone, and both fix the hidden misuses. B's creditMain walks the whole stack on every exit, so open outer scopes and outer Physics scopes get credited again on every nested exit. That inflates scope and physics times, so the physics bug is not fixed and the field meanings change. B also fails StyLua. A splits scopes across frames correctly, uses interval unions to avoid double counting, measures GPU time from GPU-thread scopes, and passes all checks.

criteria.criterion: Leaves the shared profiler as it found it
criteria.note: Never pauses capture or sets the frame limit.

Uses EnterTimestampFrameLocal and frame ends, but on every exit creditMain credits all ancestors (count = depth+1), so open outer scopes are re-added on each child exit and frames can exceed their length; underflowed exits are skipped.
Picks the outermost Physics scope per event, but adds it again on every nested exit, so Physics is still overcounted.
Uses outermost GPU-thread scopes with TickToMsGpu and clamped enters; this looks right.
Uses FetchTimerDesc/FetchGroupDesc, FetchLastCounterSample, and calls FindGroupId once with a cache.
StyLua fails on its own creditMain signature, and the inflated scope/physics numbers change the fields' meaning.

strengths: Snapshot-based and never touches global profiler state
Correct frame splitting with clamped enters
Interval union handles nested scopes and nested Physics cleanly
GPU time measured from GPU thread scopes with TickToMsGpu
Fixes all hidden misuses; all checks pass
weaknesses: No pcall, so an error leaks the session and iterator
Relies on IsFrameBoundary/TimestampGpu, which the provided facts don't document

strengths: Robust snapshot with pcall cleanup and slot reset
weaknesses: Ancestor scopes credited on every child exit, which badly inflates TopScopes and PhysicsMs
